rationale: Both independently zero in on the ground truth's central concern (unscoped vllm_c default hitting ~14 unbenchmarked diffusion models) with nearly identical model lists and the same _DIFFUSION_IR_OP_PRIORITY_FUNCS/Cosmos3 remedy, and both catch the Part1-vs-Part2 interaction and sibling-platform (ROCm/XPU) staleness. Y edges ahead on recall by also catching that Cosmos3's own override only pins two fields (leaving it partially exposed to the same flip) and by validating the accuracy-comparison ask (SSIM/PSNR) that X never addresses. Y's evidence-per-claim format (grep/arithmetic/git-log citations) is safely verifiable, whereas X's 'What I verified' section makes striking claims of executing actual CUDA kernel comparisons on named GPU hardware that are hard to trust as genuine, denting precision. Actionability is comparably strong on both sides.
